what_was_done: The three facts the finding named now each have a home, and the main restatements are gone: the record's place (artifacts/flag.md), the handling of the variables (F-KEY) and the default of flags.require (flag-config-keys.toml). Three restatements of the same kind remain, one of them added by this round. (1) config/flags.md 'Keys and local runs' still says 'The tool never reads the value of a key variable', which is F-KEY's reads cell ('Never the value of a key variable'), so 'says only what the keys name and who reads them' does not hold. (2) The rule that a person's value in [flags] wins over [flags.approved] is in three places: the header of flag-config-keys.toml (override = true, 'where it wins'), config/flags.md 'Who writes it' ('A check reads a key from [flags] when a person wrote it there and from [flags.approved] otherwise'), and, added with the D31R-C-7 change, the flags.enabled meaning ('A person's value in [flags] is the person's own answer and wins'). (3) The moved-test rule (an existing test is moved, never edited or dropped, and a pending test keeps the flag from being turned on) is in feature-flags.md 'Why it is this way' and again in flag-lifecycle.md 'Delivered off', besides its homes in the test-writer duty and F-ON. To do: delete the sentence in (1). For (2), keep the rule in config/flags.md, cut 'and wins' from the enabled meaning, and have the header say only which keys a person may also write, with a link to config:flags. For (3), keep the reason in feature-flags.md and cut the 'Delivered off' sentence down to a link to the test-writer duty and F-STATES.
